resolvedQuestions.text: What does a full load of the repository rules cost per session and per compaction window?
How does prompt caching affect input cost versus context occupancy?
What compression range is plausible, and what behavior does compression risk losing?
Which cross-lineage claims survive adversarial review?

keyFindings.label: The bare-imperative contrast rests on two prohibitions with confounds (detection ambiguity for legit tables, different base rates); directional evidence only

10 compression patterns measured: P1 bare-vs-justified (n=2 labelled), P2 pointer dedup, P3 self-check fold (high risk), P4 boilerplate, P5 frontmatter relocation, P6 AGENTS.md restatement, P7 justification tails, P8 meta, P9 triplicate collapse, P10 enumeration punctuation
keyFindings.confidence: high on bytes; low-medium on risk column

keyFindings.label: Card drops every numbered-section norm: loses measured/operative enforcement in 6 enumerated files (comm-prose semicolon ban, comm table/filler bans, blast-radius tier table, uncertainty LOGIC-SYNC+never-invent, evidence receipt/command tests, root-cause loop); holds only for umbrella files (skill-hub, answer-the-actual-request); partial for 5
Compression floor tracks rule-statement share: e-and-p (64% normative) floors near -11%, communication (43%) reaches -28%; no uniform per-file rate
communication.md draft: 11,458 -> 8,279 B (-27.8%); enforcement lost = three named edge clauses ~145 B (paragraph-step, count-line-is-not-an-item, reader-decides) + all failure-naming sentences
evidence-and-proof.md draft: 11,823 -> 10,465 B (-11.5%); enforcement loss ~zero - every tier, test, checklist and disclosure survives
Card (frontmatter+fires-when+the-rule) = 960-1,809 B/file, 18,207 total, 17.0% of corpus; sibling claim confirmed within ~2%
Rule-statement is 54.0% of corpus (57,847 B); self-check 10.2% (10,941); frontmatter 9.6% (10,246); failure-prevents 5.5% (5,909); fires-when 4.1% (4,414); examples only 1.2% (1,312)
All 13 rules decomposed into the steer parts; every file reconciles to wc -c exactly, grand total 107,092 B = evidence-pack section 1
Modelled per-rule targets total ~77,000 B (~19,250 tokens, -28%) - later falsified as uniform; see f-iter003-floor
Self-check is the outside-card part carrying enforcement: already a compressed restatement of every norm (489-1,648 B); card+checklist is a ready-made slim load
Card+checklist retains norm SHAPE not CONTENT: comm.md card+checklist ~3,030 B passes the audit items but drops the offender enumeration and re-render spec the checklist audits
Whether failure-naming sentences carry model-side motivation is UNKNOWN; both drafts drop them all and are the test artifacts for that question

keyFindings.statement: Consistency: no reopening of the advisor-pointer or trigger-index refusals; measure-before-build applies to the hook only; concision playbook stays other lineages' scope.

Must-carry set vs the smallest cap (16,384 B, ends mid-line 175): inside today - Four Laws 11-18, PLAN-WORKFLOW LOCK 20-30, Comment Hygiene 32-34, Halt Conditions 36-41, gates 49-61/70-77/79-86/93-101, Verification Standards 151-161, Final-State Verification 165-170; outside today - section 8 pointer line 261 and clauses 263, section 10 mandates 281, 285.
Reply-time five: 42,811 B all five; 18,340 B mandatory two; 29,143 B with handoff at turn end.

Part 1: AGENTS.md carries binding clauses plus pointer lines (the §8 pattern), never full rule text; stay inside the 16,384-byte guaranteed delivery budget. Falsifier: a measured prohibition that moves only when its full text is resident.
REPO RULES.md is the Gate 5 router, loaded on the first write of a session; read-only turns never fire Gate 5.
The 16,384-byte delivery cap constrains resident-card options in at least this runtime.

Option 1 status quo: resident ~6.8k tok (4.1k as delivered); per-window fixed loads router ~3.0k + brief ~65 + notice ~138, variable rule loads 6.2-8.2k per fire; silence = nothing fires; model-side dedup only; six runtimes for the brief.

Part 2: Gate 5 loads router plus matched cards, full text on demand; ~70-80% load-event reduction at measured bounds; keeps the action key and silence; no new surface. Falsifier: compliance drop, frequent card-insufficient full opens, or cards unbuildable in bands.

Part 3: no hook now; future role is action-boundary card delivery on the directive-lifecycle window model with delivered-set keying and boundary-epoch-only suppression; must not be an always-on constant. Falsifier: a measured Gate 5 miss rate with cost; or transcript evidence everywhere plus the extension built.
Option 3 Gate 5 cards: 0 resident; per-fire 0.7-1.8k tokens vs 6.2-8.2k today (~70-80% reduction); silence = no trigger match; reaches every runtime Gate 5 reaches.
Trigger-table rule files load per matched action; 3-4 files firing at once is the normal case (~24.7-33.0 KB per load event).
Option 2 resident cards: +2,509 B to +17,882 B; zero per-turn; full text on demand 1.4-3.0k per file; silence model-mediated; reset at compaction; verified delivery only Claude and Devin.

Runtime caps sourced: Claude Code no hard cap on CLAUDE.md (200-line/25KB caps apply to auto-memory MEMORY.md only); Codex project_doc_max_bytes default 32 KiB cumulative across the AGENTS.md chain (local config has no override); Devin 16,384 B observed; Cursor no enforced cap sourced (advisory 500 lines; 1k-char prerelease warning reported as visual bug); OpenCode no byte guard (entire file injected every loop; effective cap = context window); Pi UNKNOWN (no byte cap documented).

Storage: durable tmpdir store (base dir env or tmpdir()/speckit-advisor), layout directive-lifecycle/<project-hash>/<session-hash>.json plus generation/epoch/poison files; Pi globalThis map; OpenCode epoch map; spec-gate alternative under .skilled/skills/.state/spec-gate/.
Design delta: whole-payload equality is the current dedup key; 'a given rule at most once' needs a delivered-card set - new work.

Reset: compaction via boundary events from registered owners (session-prime, post-compaction, cursor precompact, codex session-start), transcript shrink, and epoch advance (null session invalidates all).
Reset-semantics mismatch: only the directive lifecycle matches 'reset only on a compaction boundary'; the spec-gate marker is session-scoped with different reset events.

Marker: directive-lifecycle receipt v2 (directives/transcriptPath/transcriptHighWaterBytes/storeGeneration/lifecycleEpoch) with proven-repeat suppression; spec-gate field naming is the naming precedent only.

Option 4 hook cards: 0 resident; measured fire count (orchestrator, 93 of 265 windows load any rule; 3.5 rules avg, median 3, p90 7) puts card delivery at ~820-1,560 tokens in loading windows, ~290-550 averaged across all windows; dedup machinery exists; transcript evidence for dedup proof UNKNOWN outside Claude.
Session-start/compaction recovery path exists; size UNKNOWN.
Advisor brief ~261 B full / ~54 B deduped per prompt; spec-gate notice 551 B once per session.

Coverage: Claude/Devin/Codex/OpenCode/Pi covered; Cursor reset covered but delivery contradicted within the contract; dedup proof needs transcript evidence or delivery stays full every turn (once-per-window not met on transcript-less runtimes).
Compaction is the observed natural window boundary: 104 re-reads after a boundary vs 1 within a window.
Gate 5 reach is partial: 14 of 44 sessions read any rule via Read (undercount).
Card-size bounds measured: index form 2,509 B total; full card proxy 17,882 B total (935-1,784 B per rule); drafted size UNKNOWN.
Inherited bounds: race can double-deliver (precedent accepts); kill switches restore full; all uncertainty fails open to full delivery.
Orchestrator's measured fire count: 93 of 265 compaction windows load any rule (35%); 3.5 distinct rules average, median 3, p90 7; supersedes the option-4 per-window UNKNOWN.
AGENTS.md reaches the model as the session rules block; in this Devin session it was delivered truncated at 16,384 bytes (about 10.6 KB not resident).
Option 5 load everything: 145,957 B / ~36.5k tokens per load; no silence; no mechanical dedup.

keyFindings.label: A full-load scenario is about 37k estimated input tokens per context window: AGENTS.md 6.8k + REPO RULES.md 3.0k + all 13 rule files 26.8k. For a session that hits Gate 5 and then a substantive reply loading the five reply rules, the measured components total about 20.5k before any other action-triggered rules. The estimate is 4 bytes per token, not tokenizer output.

If a full rule bundle is reloaded after every compaction, each later window adds about 37k tokens; if only the 13 rule bodies are re-read, it adds about 26.8k. The evidence pack counts 104 post-compaction rule re-reads after compaction boundaries, but does not provide each window's file mix or size, so actual cumulative per-session reload cost is UNKNOWN.

API prompt caching can discount repeated input and reuse cached KV state for an unchanged prefix; it does not itself shorten the prompt. Inference: cached input cost and context occupancy are separate. This Codex invocation's actual cache-hit rate, context limit, and price for gpt-6-luna are UNKNOWN.

A measured 4,984-byte slice of the existing router trigger table is 95.3% smaller by bytes than the 107,092-byte rule corpus, but it is only a route-and-summary proxy. ASSUMPTION: applying the 935-1,784-byte card-size bounds named in steer.md to each of 13 files implies 78.4-88.6% fewer corpus bytes; no rendered-token or behavior-preservation test supports that range.

The current evidence does not establish that full loading improves compliance broadly: table use is 20.3% after reading communication.md versus 11.6% in never-read sessions, while semicolon use is 17.0% after reading communication-prose.md versus 43.7% in never-read sessions. Pattern-based detection and non-randomized sessions limit causal interpretation.

Whether a blanket 37k-token load is affordable for this model/runtime is UNKNOWN: the evidence pack estimates text size but supplies neither gpt-6-luna's usable context window nor Codex billing/cache telemetry.

F24's measured card-size savings may be real, but card-only content drops numbered-body norms in 6 of 13 rules and is partial in 5; the missing semicolon ban is the only observed rule with a read-associated reduction. The 'no measurement needed to start' conclusion is unsafe for a default rollout. Verdict: weakened.

F23's pointer pattern is a sound routing shape, but 'already working' is not established: answer-the-actual-request.md appears in 4 of 82 shell-inclusive session reads, without an opportunity denominator, and another lineage reports an observed 16,384-byte delivery cut before AGENTS.md:261. Verdict: weakened.

F25's wait-for-a-measured-Gate-5-miss rule stands. The 104 post-compaction re-reads and four answer-rule reads are counts, not opportunity-adjusted proof that a needed rule was missed; prior research recommends a logging-only observer first. Verdict: stands.

The table claim is descriptive for long, no-tool replies in this sample, not a causal estimate: the after rate is 20.3% of 1,063 replies and never is 11.6% of 86, but the cohorts are not randomized and the table regex flags requested document tables. Verdict: weakened.

The two observations do not support a causal rule that shorter literal prohibitions bind better: a punctuation ban and a table ban differ in rule, task exposure, baseline rate, exception structure, and sample sizes, and neither was randomized. Verdict: refuted as a causal inference; retained only as a hypothesis.

On the card conflict, the evidence supports the loss warning over wholesale card-only rollout: the proposed card omits numbered body rules in 6 files, including No semicolon, and is partial in 5. A card plus all self-checks would still be about 72.8% fewer bytes by calculation, but its behavior effect remains unmeasured. Verdict: weakened for F24's cost claim; the card-only safety claim is refuted.

A response linter could be cause-independent only if it can prevent or repair the delivered reply with a low-false-positive predicate. The current Claude Stop completion hook is async, completion-claim-specific, advisory-only, and returns approve; a pipe-table check also flags requested tables unless it reads the request and exceptions. We and luna-compliance used the same gpt-6-luna model ID, so my agreement on the false-positive and enforcement caveats is not independent-model corroboration. Verdict: weakened.
